s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiac arrest with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and hemodynamic collapse
salient_findings: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
key_facts: 34-year-old White woman with a history of obesity
Presented after an unwitnessed cardiac arrest
Required mechanical intubation for airway protection
Developed atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
Experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions
Troponin T: 0.847 µg/L (elevated)
Troponin I: 0.13 ng/mL (elevated)
Urine toxicology, alcohol, and acetaminophen screening results were negative
ECG showed sinus tachycardia with heart rate 101 beats/min, QTc 443 ms
Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal biventricular size and function
Diagnostic coronary angiogram: no obstructive coronary artery disease
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: mild left ventricular and left atrial dilation, preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (62%)
Electroencephalogram showed status epilepticus

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and hemodynamic collapse

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc 443 ms and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular fibrillation with no clear cause

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular tachycardia and possible right ventricular involvement

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and possible myocardial dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is a hallmark of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. The normal cardiac structure and function, as well as the absence of other explanatory conditions, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc interval was mildly prolonged but not significantly so, and the clinical presentation was more consistent with a primary ventricular arrhythmia disorder.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: The presence of a clear trigger for the ventricular tachycardia (premature ventricular contractions) suggests a more specific underlying condition.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The cardiac imaging studies did not show evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or fibrofatty replacement.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The echocardiogram and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging did not show evidence of left ventricular hypertrophy or outflow tract obstruction.
